fields.System.Title: INT-2 — Outbound integration
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Tell the ERP what happened in the warehouse, reliably, without letting a slow or absent ERP
affect warehouse work.

Scope

In. Publishing receipt, shipment, and adjustment confirmations; retry and dead-letter.

Out. The outbox mechanism itself — that is [FDN-8](../FDN/FDN-8-outbox.md). This feature is
the payloads and the consumers.

Design notes

Everything goes through the outbox. A direct call inside the stock transaction means a slow
ERP slows receiving, an ERP outage stops receiving, and a successful call followed by a
rollback leaves the ERP believing something that never happened.

Ordering matters per aggregate. A shipment confirmation must not overtake the receipt
confirmation for the same stock. Deliver in sequence per aggregate, and have consumers reject
out-of-order events rather than applying them.

The consumer must deduplicate on event_id. At-least-once delivery is the guarantee;
exactly-once does not exist. Document this explicitly to whoever builds the ERP side — it is
easy for them to assume otherwise, and the result is double invoicing.

INT-203 has financial consequences. A stock adjustment changes the value of what the
business holds. Publish it, and make sure the payload carries the reason code so the ERP can
post it correctly.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Event published before commit | [doc 09 §2.4](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Event delivered twice to a non-idempotent consumer | [doc 09 §3.4](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Events delivered out of order | [doc 08 §10](../../../docs/08-data-sync-and-migrations.md) |
| Consumer failing permanently, backlog growing | [doc 04 §3.1](../../../docs/04-modules.md) |
